# Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL)

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-29 · status **complete** · Budget spent after covering identity, CSR policy, FY2024-25 project-wise expenditure, annual report CSR narrative, and one secondary academic source; sufficient to answer all six questions.

Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) is a public-sector oil refinery headquartered at Golaghat district, Assam, set up under the provisions of the Assam Accord. It was historically a BPCL subsidiary; as of the FY2023-24 Annual Report its shareholders are Oil India Limited, Government of Assam and Engineers India Limited (Oil India acquired BPCL's 54.16% stake), and Wikipedia describes it as now a division of Oil India Limited under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Government of India. NRL's CSR and Sustainability Policy explicitly ties its CSR mandate to the Assam Accord genesis and designates a 10km radius around its Numaligarh refinery and Siliguri terminal as 'local area' entitled to ~60% of CSR spend. The FY2024-25 project-wise CSR expenditure disclosure (145+ line items) shows CSR overwhelmingly concentrated in Assam, especially Golaghat district (site of the refinery), with health care, education, skill development, sports, rural infrastructure, sanitation, drinking water, gender/disability support, environment/wildlife conservation, and arts & culture as recurring activity heads. One confirmed Nagaland project (a children's park in Mokokchung) and one Meghalaya-beneficiary skill-development project were found; no Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura or Mizoram projects appear in the FY2024-25 filing. A 2022 academic paper (low confidence, self-reported survey data, not an NRL disclosure) corroborates that NRL's CSR footprint centres on a 10km radius around the refinery and reports high community awareness/benefit levels. CIN was not located in the sources read within budget. No project was found located in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, or Mizoram, and no NRL statement was found explicitly naming 'Northeast India' as a strategic region beyond the Assam/Golaghat local-area framing tied to the Assam Accord. Also flagged: search results surfaced groupnrl.in and nrl.co.uk ('NRL Group'), a UK recruitment/staffing company unrelated to Numaligarh Refinery Limited; these were not used as sources.

Website: https://www.nrl.co.in

## Where the work ran

- **Local area definition for CSR**: 10 km radius of Numaligarh refinery (Golaghat, Assam) and Siliguri marketing terminal designated as 'local area'; ~60% of CSR budget earmarked there
  > Focus of NRL's CSR and Sustainability activities shall be in the area within 10 km radius of the refinery at Numaligarh and the Company's marketing terminal at Siliguri. These two areas shall be deemed as 'local areas'... Around 60% of the total CSR and sustainability budget would be spent in the local area.
  <sub>source · https://www.nrl.co.in/upload/TopMenuFile/TOPSUBMENU35444MainMenuEnglishLevel-2_CSR_Policy_Rev1.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Rural health infrastructure upgrade, Golaghat District, Assam (FY2023-24)** (FY2023-24): Renovation/equipment for 40 hospitals and 8 Public Health Centres in Golaghat District
  > The Company walked the extra mile to improve the rural health infrastructure by renovating and providing medical equipment to 40 Hospitals and 8 Public Health Centres in Golaghat District of Assam, as a primary healthcare intervention measure.
  <sub>source · https://www.nrl.co.in/upload/NRL_Annual_Report_2023-24_12082024.pdf · confidence high</sub>

## Programmes

- **CSR Vision statement**: To pursue CSR and Sustainability activities with a difference for ushering in inclusive development of the community
  > Vision: The CSR and sustainability Vision shall be: "To pursue CSR and Sustainability activities with a difference for ushering in inclusive development of the community".
  <sub>source · https://www.nrl.co.in/upload/TopMenuFile/TOPSUBMENU35444MainMenuEnglishLevel-2_CSR_Policy_Rev1.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Five broad CSR activity heads**: (a) Livelihood Generation, (b) Promotion of Education and Skill Development, (c) Infrastructure Development, (d) Promotion of Health Care, (e) Promotion of Arts, Sports, Literature and Culture
  > CSR and Sustainability activities of NRL is to be pursued along five broad-heads, viz. (a) Livelihood Generation, (b) Promotion of Education and Skill Development, (c) Infrastructure Development, (d) Promotion of Health Care (e) Promotion of Arts, Sports, Literature and Culture...
  <sub>source · https://www.nrl.co.in/upload/TopMenuFile/TOPSUBMENU35444MainMenuEnglishLevel-2_CSR_Policy_Rev1.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Flagship CSR schemes**: Niramoy (healthcare), Prerona (girl-child education), Parichannata (toilet blocks), Xokha (assistance to differently-abled)
  > NRL's flagship schemes such as 'Niramoy' on healthcare, 'Prerona' on girl-child education, 'Parichannata' on construction of toilet blocks, 'Xokha' for assistance to differently-abled persons, among others, shall continue to be pursued with increased emphasis.
  <sub>source · https://www.nrl.co.in/upload/TopMenuFile/TOPSUBMENU35444MainMenuEnglishLevel-2_CSR_Policy_Rev1.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **FY2024-25 thematic CSR focus** (FY2024-25): Health & Nutrition (60% of outlay, Rs. 5070.00 Lakhs of a total budget of Rs. 8450.00 Lakhs)
  > As per DPE guidelines, 'Health & Nutrition' is the Thematic Focus Area of CSR for the Financial Year 2024-25. Accordingly, 60% of the outlay amounting to Rs. 5070.00 Lakhs has been earmarked for the promotion of health & provision of nutritional food items for various sections of society.
  <sub>source · https://www.nrl.co.in/upload/nrlCSR_Annual_Plan_24-25.pdf · confidence high</sub>
